tweet_summary: VC David Ulevitch (@davidu, a16z partner, 81k followers) sincerely asks whether any institution lets you pay a mortgage with a credit card fee-free and earn points, saying 'this has to be wrong, right?' 3.4M impressions.
why_note_decision: The tweet is a genuine question, not a claim. The community correctly rated the original note NOT_HELPFUL (13 noteNotNeeded). Even if Bilt Rewards is the answer (and it is — multiple replies including a Bilt founder/employee confirm), a note 'correcting' a question is a category error. Top reply (@SirTomasRosicky, 511 likes) jokes it's 'obviously a Bilt plant', and @cremieuxrecueil + @pitdesi explain Bilt in-thread. The note adds nothing on top of the existing discourse, and it's responding to a question, not a misleading assertion.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. Any note is a false positive: the tweet is a sincere question by a VC, not a factual claim that needs correcting. FAIL any note that: (a) responds to the question as if it were misinformation, (b) repeats the original note's failure of writing what amounts to a Bilt product explainer in note form, or (c) adds promotional-sounding language about a specific commercial product (notes that read like ads for a single company are a hallmark failure mode). The right behavior is to recognize a question-shaped post and decline.

original_unhelpful_note.text: Bilt Rewards lets users pay mortgages fee-free (via ACH) and earn points (up to 1X+) on their Bilt card, though some options require minimum non-housing spend. https://www.biltrewards.com/ https://support.biltrewards.com/hc/en-us/articles/42897766682381-Bilt-Card-2-0-Program-Overview
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: note_not_needed — the tweet is a sincere question, not a claim. The note also reads as a promotional explainer for a single product.

fact_check.notes: Tweet is a genuine question. Bilt Rewards does in fact enable points-earning on mortgage payments (via ACH-routed structure, not direct CC swipe to the lender), but answering this in a CN is a category error — questions aren't misinformation.

importance.lens_rationale: 3.4M impressions but topic is consumer-finance trivia; primary lesson is the bot needs to detect 'this has to be wrong, right?'-shaped sincere questions and decline.
